subject: comparison of hand-coded model to rstanarm

messages.author: de6fb7786d893b5c
messages.subject: comparison of hand-coded model to rstanarm
parts:
Hi all,

I'm trying to figure out why I'm getting a slightly different set of results from a simple model coded in rstanarm vs. one that I wrote myself. I have data on GPA for about 1200 students. The median number of measurements per student is 8, with a maximum of 12, and a handful for whom we have fewer than 8 because they left the district or dropped out or something. I've estimated a simple hierarchical, random intercept model like so:

data {
  int<lower=1> n; //number of obs
  int<lower=1> p; //number of participants
  vector[n] y; // observed vals
  int s[p]; //number of obs per participant
  int sub_obs[n]; //subject observation indicator
}
parameters {
  vector[p] b_mu; //mean for student p
  vector<lower=0>[p] sigma_i; //variance for student p
  real<lower=0> sigma; //one grand sigma 
  real mu;  //sampled grand mean

}

model {
  int pos;
  mu ~ normal(0,1);
  sigma_i ~ normal(0,1);
  b_mu ~ normal(mu, sigma);

  pos <- 1;
  for (i in 1:p){
    y[pos:pos+s[i]] ~ normal(b_mu[i], sigma_i[i]);
    pos <- pos+s[i];
  }
}

This appears to work really well - all three chains run in under a minute, there are no troublesome divergence warnings like a few other models I've tried, the chains look good, effective sample sizes, Rhats, etc don't raise any red flags. Further, the estimates are in line with what I'd expect - the median of the posterior for `mu` is 2.76, [2.71-2.80].

When I run what I assume is the same model in rstanarm:

stan_glmer(overallgpa ~ 1 + (1|ID), data=df.mod, prior_intercept=normal(0,1))


things are a bit different. It runs quite a bit more slowly (around 6 minutes per chain), and the estimates across multiple runs are consistently lower (median of `mu` is 2.69, [2.64-2.75]), and there are some troublesome diagnostics - high autocorrelation in the chains, low n_eff & Rhat > 1.01 for mu, and so on. My best guess is that rstanarm uses non-centered parameterizations by default, and this particular model happens to fall on the left-hand side of figures 8 and 9 in Betancourt & Girolami. I tried looking at the rstanarm code produced from the model, but it's a bit too hairy to make much sense of without some serious effort on my part.

Any guidance here would be much appreciated!

-Travis

Ben
